value.title: dd — friction ledger
value.note: Things that made dd harder to use than it should be, reported by REAL CONSUMERS driving it in repos that are not this one. Opened 2026-08-08 on Jordan's ask, as a sibling to the wishlist — deliberately separate, because a wishlist row is work someone wants and a friction row is EVIDENCE someone hit. Only some evidence becomes work, and the ledger is worth more if that conversion is a decision rather than an assumption. Jordan routes dd frictions here from other fleets. A row stays open until it is fixed, ruled wontfix, or fails to reproduce — never because it got old.

value.title: builder schema packages exist ONLY in harness-engineering, and the CLI's own remediation for the miss is a dead end
value.what_happened: First command in a consuming repo. `harness plan new <slug>` writes plan.dd.json and assets/tasks/phase-1/tasks.dd.json, then FAILS to render either sibling: 'schema "builder/plan" was not found in any discovery root'. All four discovery roots probed and empty — <plandir>, <repo>/.dd, <repo>/.harness/.dd, ~/.dd. The builder schema packages exist only in harness-engineering/.dd/schemas/, and there are FIVE of them: plan, backpressure, execution-log, fence, review. Net effect: dd-native /builder plan works in harness-engineering and in no other repo.
value.workaround: cp -R ~/substrate/harness-engineering/.dd/schemas/builder ./.dd/schemas/ — after which plan render and dd set both work.
value.asked_for: Seed the schema packages on `plan new` — pij-massive-meadowlark's recommendation, and it stays inside the documented four-root precedence rather than adding a fifth bundled root. (Shipping them inside the package as a new root is the alternative; it keeps schemas versioned with the code that reads them, but changes resolution order for every consumer.)
value.independently_hit_by: pij-mental-dajeil, 2026-08-07, plan 001 — captured as DL-002 with the same workaround (hand-copied the builder family out of harness-engineering) and the same diagnosis (no `harness dd schema install`, no ship-with-CLI mechanism). Two fleets, two repos, identical wall.
value.note: CONFIRMED rather than merely open: hit independently by two agents in two repos before either knew of the other. That is as strong as a friction report gets. It also bears directly on plan 002 — an SDK that cannot resolve its own first-party schemas in a consuming repo is not consumable, whichever distribution method ships it. Candidate shapes, not yet ruled: ship the schemas inside the package and add them as a discovery root; or a `dd schema install <family>` verb; or seed on first use. The first keeps them versioned with the code that reads them, which argues for it. CORRECTION 2026-08-08, and the correcting reporter is the one who caught it: ox first said SIX packages including builder/tasks. There is no builder/tasks — assets/tasks/phase-N/tasks.dd.json declares schema 'builder/plan' and uses its `tasks` and `done_when` sections. Re-derived independently by pij-massive-meadowlark and again here (`ls .dd/schemas/builder` → five; the task file's own `dd.schema` field → builder/plan). I had TRANSCRIBED ox's six into this row without deriving it, which is the plan-001 class arriving in a friction ledger.

value.title: 16 of builder/plan's 22 declared sections can never be created — the section set is frozen at scaffold time
value.what_happened: builder/plan declares 22 sections; `harness plan new` scaffolds only 6 (meta, summary, goals, non_goals, acceptance_criteria, phases). The other 16 — testing_strategy, documentation_strategy, key_findings, gate_matrix, risks, risks_assumptions, open_questions, clarifications, planning_seam, acceptance_coverage, implementation_summary, execution_guardrails, research_context, workshop_opportunities, tasks, done_when — CANNOT BE CREATED. `dd set` and `dd add` both refuse with E450 section-unknown ('the document has no section X'), and there is no add-section verb: dd has get/set/add/rm, and `rm` can DELETE a section but nothing creates one. So the section set is frozen at scaffold time, permanently.
value.workaround: Hand-edit plan.dd.json then `harness dd build` — which the builder skill explicitly forbids ('never hand-edit plan.dd.json'), even though the dd README sanctions it. So the only escape route is one the calling skill prohibits.
value.asked_for: Either `plan new` scaffolds every declared section empty, or set/add auto-create a schema-DECLARED section. E450 should fire only for sections the SCHEMA does not declare — not for ones the document merely lacks.
value.independently_hit_by: pij-mental-dajeil, 2026-08-07, plan 001 — captured as DL-003, same 6-of-22 count, same E450, same conclusion that no verb can add a section. Workaround used there was a structural JSON insert of empty sections followed immediately by plan validate + render to prove schema-validity and no drift.
value.note: The sharpest part of ox's report is the one I did not make: this DIRECTLY BREAKS /builder 1b plan, whose module instructs the agent to author key_findings, gate_matrix, clarifications, planning_seam, testing_strategy, risks and open_questions — none of which dd can hold. So a skill and a tool that ship together disagree about what is possible, and the only bridge between them is an action one of them forbids. E450's message is also arguably the real defect: 'the document has no section X' is TRUE and useless, because it describes the document when the actionable fact is whether the SCHEMA allows X. An error that names the wrong authority sends the reader to the wrong fix.

value.title: `dd schema list` reports ok with zero schemas — the repo's own never-fake-success rule, violated by the repo
value.reported_by: pij-disturbing-ox (under-sold in its own report); proven here by pij-mental-dajeil
value.reported_from: chainglass dogfood → re-derived in a clean scratch repo
value.what_happened: When `builder/plan` fails to resolve, acts/plan/index.ts:298 tells the reader to run `harness dd schema list` to see which roots are searched. In a repo with no schemas that command returns `status: ok`, `schemas: []`, three roots — and `next_action: "Run `dd schema show <name>` for one schema in full."`, which points at the set it has just proven empty. So the CLI's own remediation path is a DEAD END BY CONSTRUCTION: it reports success on a state that is definitionally unconfigured, and hands the reader an instruction that cannot be followed.
value.workaround: None needed for the reader who already knows the answer; there is none for the reader who does not, which is the entire point.
value.asked_for: Zero resolving schemas is `unconfigured` (exit 2), not `ok` — and the next_action should name how to GET schemas, not how to inspect the none that exist. The roots list is the right evidence to print; the verdict and the next step are the defects.
value.independently_hit_by: Proven directly rather than reported: `git init` in an empty dir, then `dd schema list --json` from this repo's bin. Re-derive with exactly that.
value.note: THIS IS OUR OWN HEADLINE RULE BROKEN BY OUR OWN CLI. AGENTS.md and orient-local both state it: 'unconfigured means nothing is mapped here yet, never it worked — the repo's green-but-wrong defence, enforced in code, not prose.' Zero schemas resolving IS nothing-mapped-here-yet, and the verb returns ok. Same family as a probe that cannot detect and a gate that cannot fail: an instrument that answers confidently about a question it did not actually examine. Found by following ox's lead on a point it explicitly said it had under-sold — worth noting, because the sharpest finding in a report is not always the one the reporter leads with.

value.title: The backpressure seam is not dd-aware — the survey and the plan cannot link to each other
value.what_happened: eng-harness-flow's backpressure verb module declares Consumes: docs/plans/<ord>-<slug>/<slug>-plan.md and Produces: assets/backpressure-coverage.md. In a dd-native plan folder that consumed file DOES NOT EXIST — the plan is plan.dd.json plus a generated plan.dd.md — and the module's PHASE 0 step 1 says 'If neither exists, there is nothing to survey against; say so and STOP.' So an agent following the module literally STOPS on every dd-native plan. Worse, the artifact it is told to produce is MARKDOWN, while builder/plan's `pressure` fields target builder/backpressure/section/rows — so a markdown survey can never be linked from an acceptance criterion or a done_when assertion.
value.workaround: Authored BOTH: assets/backpressure.dd.json (authoritative, 11 rows, pressure-linked from all 8 ACs and all 16 done_when assertions) plus the markdown the module contractually requires. Two artifacts, one truth, maintained by hand.
value.asked_for: The verb should consume plan.dd.json and emit backpressure.dd.json, with the markdown as its GENERATED sibling.
value.independently_hit_by: Not yet — this repo's plan 001 never ran the backpressure seam against a dd-native plan, so the wall was never reached here.
value.note: ox's own closing line is the finding: two artifacts, one truth, maintained by hand — EXACTLY THE DRIFT dd EXISTS TO KILL. The seam that is supposed to establish how done-ness will be proved is itself unproved against the document format the same toolchain produces. Note the shape it shares with fr-0002: a skill and a tool that ship together disagree about what exists, and the agent is left to bridge them by hand. That is now twice, which makes it a pattern rather than an incident — the dd-native and markdown-native halves of the builder toolchain were specified against different realities.

value.title: builder/backpressure schema and the backpressure module disagree on vocabulary, silently
value.reported_from: chainglass, dd-builder dogfood — filed because the o-prime asked for the one nearly not filed
value.what_happened: builder/backpressure/schema.json declares certainty enum [Partial, Confident, Proven] and proof_tier enum [computational, human-judgement]. The backpressure verb module specifies certainty Strong|Partial|Weak (STEP 4 — three named rungs with explicit definitions) and three tiers computational|inferential|human-judgement. So 'Strong' and 'Weak' — two of the module's three verdicts — are UNREPRESENTABLE in the dd document, and 'inferential', which the module names as its own middle tier and uses throughout, does not exist in the schema.
value.workaround: Landed on Partial, which validated only BY COINCIDENCE — it is the one value both vocabularies happen to share.
value.asked_for: Reconcile the two, and pick a direction deliberately. The module's three-rung certainty is load-bearing prose (it drives the closing verdict's four-rung ladder); the schema's Confident/Proven have no definition anywhere ox could find.
value.note: THE FAILURE MODE IS THE TIMING, and it is why this outranks its severity label: a survey reaching a STRONG verdict would have been refused by the schema AFTER the analysis was already done, with no way to record the conclusion it had reached. The tool does not prevent the wrong answer — it prevents recording the right one, and only at the end. That is worse than a validation error at the start, because the cost is paid in work already completed. Two vocabularies for one concept, in a toolchain whose entire premise is single-definition — the same two-vocabularies hazard this repo used to argue plan/ should not be split across two codebases. ox nearly did not file this one; it is the sharpest of the four.

value.title: dd-rendered plans break every downstream consumer that scrapes per-phase headings — SILENTLY
value.what_happened: The legacy markdown plan contract emits '#### Phase Index' plus a '#### Phase N: <Title>' block per phase, and downstream tooling extracts by that heading. builder/plan's renderer instead emits ONE '## Phases' section containing a TABLE — no per-phase heading exists at any level. flow-pair's ContextPackCompiler.extractSection matches a heading by exact / prefix-colon / prefix-space and captures to the next same-or-higher heading; with --phase 'Phase 1: Implementation' it returns {ok:false, section not found} against a dd plan. So a delegation packet COMPILES WITH THE PLAN SECTION MISSING, and the miss is recorded only as an exclusion. The same assumption sits in builder's own 20-plan and 50-phase-tasks modules, which describe per-phase blocks as the output contract.
value.workaround: --phase 'Phases' (matches the table section) plus --tasks-dir, since tasks.dd.md DOES render per-task '### tk-NNNN' headings under '## Done when'.
value.asked_for: Either the plan renderer emits a per-phase heading block alongside the index table, or the consumers move to ADDRESSING ROWS (plan.dd.json#phases/ph-0001) instead of scraping headings. ox's own read, and it is right: the second is the whole point of dd.
value.independently_hit_by: Adjacent hit here, plan 001, DL-005 (2026-08-07): flow-pair's context-pack compiler reported '(no tasks found)' for a dd-format plan because it globs tasks.md while dd repos render tasks.dd.md — same compiler, same class, different file. So the compiler has now missed dd content twice by scraping for markdown shapes dd does not emit.
value.note: THE SEVERITY IS THE SILENCE, NOT THE MISS. It does not error loudly — the worker simply gets less context than the orchestrator believes it sent, and the only trace is an exclusion line nobody reads. An orchestrator cannot tell a well-briefed worker from a starved one, so a bad outcome downstream looks like a bad worker. That is the reports-success-while-broken family, and it is the third instance in this ledger (fr-0003 returns ok on zero schemas; fr-0005 refuses the right answer only at the end). ox's closing line is the sharpest thing in the whole ledger and it names what plan 002 is for: THE GRAPH EXISTS WHILE THE CONSUMER STILL SCRAPES. dd's entire premise is that structure is addressable — plan.dd.json#phases/ph-0001 is exact, stable and typed, while a heading match is a guess about layout. Every consumer still scraping is a consumer that has not been given a reason to stop, and giving them that reason IS the SDK. This row is therefore a plan-002 design input, not merely a bug.
